name: Saints Cletus and Marcellinus
history: Two popes kept on one day. Cletus, also called Anacletus, was the third bishop of Rome after Peter and Linus, and is named in the Roman Canon. Marcellinus led the Roman Church from 296 to 304, as the great persecution under Diocletian broke out, and died in or soon after it. Both are honoured by tradition as martyrs.
life: Saint Irenaeus, writing around 180, lists the bishops of Rome from the apostles: Linus, then Anacletus, then Clement. That is almost all we know of Cletus, but it is a great deal: he stood in the line of those who kept the faith handed on by Peter and Paul, and the Church names him every day in the Roman Canon. Marcellinus became pope in 296. In 303 Diocletian ordered churches destroyed, the Scriptures burned and Christians compelled to sacrifice. Later sources say that Marcellinus gave way under pressure and offered incense, then repented and died a martyr; others say nothing of a lapse, and historians are uncertain. He was buried in the catacomb of Priscilla. Whatever the truth, his story as the Church has told it is one of weakness and mercy, and of a shepherd who came back.
prayerTo: Saints Cletus and Marcellinus, shepherds of Rome in its first centuries, you handed on the faith of the apostles in times of danger. Pray for the Pope and for all who are tempted to give way under pressure. If I fall, help me to rise again quickly and return to Christ. Amen.
penance: Make a good examination of conscience today and, if you can, go to Confession. Pray for any Christian who has given up the faith under pressure.
meditation: The Church names Cletus every day in the Roman Canon, and we know almost nothing else about him. Can you be content to be faithful and unknown?
prayer: Look forgivingly on thy flock, Eternal Shepherd, and keep it in thy constant protection, by the intercession of blessed N. thy Sovereign Pontiff, whom thou didst constitute Shepherd of the whole Church. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
